summary.headline: Cera Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.4% YoY to INR 644 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 15.2% from 18.3% on brass costs and trade discounts.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11.4% YoY to INR 644 crore, led by volume (about 12%), with management citing early retail recovery from Q3 and continued project strength. EBITDA excluding other income fell to INR 98 crore (15.2% margin) from INR 106 crore (18.3%), driven by brass input costs, elevated trade discounts and pre-operating costs for Senator and Polipluz. Price increases were taken in March (11% effective) and April-May (surcharge then 8% sanitaryware and 5% faucetware), with management targeting a 14-15% EBITDA margin. Morbi gas disruptions were cited as an opportunity, with Cera running inventory and internalising outsourced SKUs. FY26 revenue was INR 2,050 crore, and FY27 guidance is 18-20% growth.

segments.name: Sanitaryware
segments.commentary: 46% of Q4 revenue, up 10.7% YoY; capacity utilisation 70% in March. Outsourcing about 60% of sanitaryware volume, mostly from Morbi. One kiln closed in March and kept closed in April.

segments.name: Faucetware
segments.commentary: 43% of Q4 revenue, up 24.3% YoY; utilisation 106% in Q4. Output of 4.3 lakh pieces/month in March; capacity moves to 5 lakh pieces/month from Q4 FY27 at about INR 4-5 crore capex. Outsourcing about 46%.

segments.name: Tiles
segments.commentary: 9% of Q4 revenue, down 8.3% YoY. Almost fully outsourced, so Q1 FY27 expected to be impacted by Morbi supply.

segments.name: Senator and Polipluz (new brands)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 19 crore (Senator about INR 10.5 crore, Polipluz about INR 8.5 crore); FY26 combined losses about INR 8.5 crore. FY27 target INR 70-80 crore; 40 Senator stores to become 60, Polipluz to grow to 200 distributors and 2,000 dealers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 overall revenue growth guided at 18-20%: sanitaryware about 12% (volume 7%, price 5-6%), faucetware about 18% (volume 10-12%, price about 8%).
Tiles and construction chemicals expected to contribute about INR 250 crore in FY27 with 20%-plus growth once Morbi supply normalises; Senator and Polipluz INR 70-80 crore.
EBITDA margin expected to sustain at about 14-15% as discounts are controlled from Q1 FY27.
Employee costs expected to rise about 10% in FY27; a pending labour long-term settlement could add wage cost.

FY27 capex about INR 43-45 crore (routine about INR 25-30 crore, faucetware INR 5 crore, office space about INR 15 crore). Greenfield plant first phase estimated at about INR 150 crore, with construction timing dependent on demand.

Senator publicity expected at INR 10-12 crore in FY27; Senator and Polipluz salary cost about INR 15.5-16 crore, with the sub-brand portfolio expected to turn profitable after publicity in FY28 per management.
capex_capacity: Faucetware capacity to rise from 4.3 lakh to 5 lakh pieces/month by debottlenecking the brownfield setup, at about INR 4-5 crore capex, operational from Q4 FY27.
Sanitaryware utilisation about 70-75% in March-April; one kiln closed in March and kept closed in April, with the second kiln expected to restart soon.

Greenfield sanitaryware plant: land of INR 27 crore already bought; first phase now estimated at about INR 150 crore (vs INR 130 crore earlier) with construction timing to be decided in coming quarters.
Internalisation of sanitaryware categories previously sourced from Morbi, expected to be available for sale from Q2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Management says retail demand improved from Q3 FY26, continued through Q4 and into April 2026; project share has risen from about 30% to 39-40% and is expected to stabilise, with a 60:40 retail-to-project split.

Price actions: 11% effective March 1 (faucetware and sanitaryware); April surcharge of 10% sanitaryware and 5% faucetware; then removed and replaced by 8% sanitaryware and 5% faucetware price increase. Management says the two-month effective increase is 12% for sanitaryware and 16% for faucetware, applied to retail; projects keep old prices for up to one year from booking.

Brass prices up about 29-30% YoY, moving from late INR 600s to INR 800-850 per kg range (as stated). Management says the 16% faucetware price increase covers about 18% COGS impact, leaving a 1-2% gap to be recovered through discount control.
Q4 volume-led growth: volume about 12%, product mix 3-4%, price/discount drag about 3%. Product mix: premium 41%, mid 38%, entry 21%. Tier-3 40%, Tier-1 36%, Tier-2 24%.
Peers' price increases reportedly 16-18% for faucets and 10-12% for sanitaryware; management says Cera is in line.

qa_highlights.question: How is retail demand likely to evolve in FY27, and what is the institution-versus-retail balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retail recovered from Q3 and continued into April, and project share rose from about 30% to 39-40%. It expects a stable 60:40 retail-to-project mix and FY27 volume growth of 7-8% for sanitaryware and 10-12% for faucetware.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the price increase delayed, and how much more is needed to protect the margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Brass rose from late INR 600s to INR 800-850 per kg with about 29-30% YoY. Cera has taken about 12% on sanitaryware and 16% on faucetware over two months, with project pricing lagging by about six months. The remaining 1-2% gap is expected to be recovered through discounts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Senator and Polipluz revenue, target and breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 revenue was about INR 19 crore (Senator 10.5, Polipluz 8.5), with a FY27 target of INR 70-80 crore. Management said the brands make a small profit before publicity and expect to be profitable after publicity next year.

qa_highlights.question: How does 18-20% overall growth reconcile with 12% sanitaryware and 18% faucetware growth?
qa_highlights.answer: The balance comes from tiles and construction chemicals (about INR 250 crore, 20%-plus growth once Morbi normalises) and Senator/Polipluz (INR 70-80 crore).

qa_highlights.question: Why are trade discounts still high when retail demand is recovering, and what is the margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said discounts rose through the downturn and cannot be cut immediately; control starts from Q1 FY27. Q4 margin rose to 15.2% from 10.2% in Q3, and management expects 14-15% to be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sanitaryware capacity utilisation, inventory and supply outlook for Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanitaryware utilisation was 70% in March; one kiln was closed. Management said inventory covers about 2-3 months of forecast demand, and tiles are expected to be impacted in Q1 because they are fully outsourced.

qa_highlights.question: What are the employee cost trends and capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Q3 included about INR 5 crore of wage code provision, and Q4 had a INR 10 crore exceptional write-back on gratuity and PL liability. Employee cost is expected to rise about 10% in FY27. Capex is guided at about INR 43-45 crore including office space of about INR 15 crore.

risks_watch: Morbi gas-driven supply disruption: sanitaryware outsourcing is about 60% (mostly Morbi) and tiles are almost fully outsourced; management expects Q1 FY27 tiles to be impacted and Morbi sanitaryware output to stay slow through monsoon, with internalised SKUs only available from Q2 FY27.

Price-cost gap: management says the 16% faucetware and 12% sanitaryware price increases cover brass costs only partly (about 1-2% gap on faucetware), and project pricing lags by about six months since projects keep old prices for up to a year from booking.
Trade discounts: margin recovery to 14-15% depends on discount control starting Q1 FY27; Q4 margin was 15.2% versus 10.2% in Q3, and Q4 benefited from inventory liquidation during Morbi disruption.

FY27 growth bridge: 18-20% overall growth relies on tiles and construction chemicals (about INR 250 crore, 20%-plus growth) and Senator/Polipluz (INR 70-80 crore) versus FY26 Senator/Polipluz revenue of about INR 19 crore and losses of about INR 8.5 crore; sustained losses and publicity spend (INR 10-12 crore) are a watch item.

Cost and capex items to track: pending labour long-term settlement could add wage cost on top of about 10% employee cost rise; greenfield sanitaryware first phase now about INR 150 crore with construction timing undecided; sanitaryware utilisation at 70-75% and second kiln restart timing.
key_quotes: Since Q3 of the current financial year, we have started seeing an improvement in the retail demand, and we saw this sustaining through Q4 also.
So, these trade discounts are again can be corrected it in the coming quarters.
Tiles will be impacted, because in the month of March, also later part of March, most of it is dependent upon outsourcing.
So, we anticipate that the current situation would be playing well for us going forward in Q1 and Q2.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on demand recovery and volume guidance, citing retail improvement from Q3 through April 2026, but was noticeably cautious on margins and Morbi-linked supply, repeatedly saying discount control is a gradual journey starting Q1 FY27. Answers on the FY27 growth bridge and Senator/Polipluz breakeven were direct, though several figures (capex total, Senator/Polipluz revenue split) were restated during Q&A.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 18-20% (sanitaryware ~12%, faucetware ~18%), backed by price increases of 8-16%, faucetware debottlenecking to 5 lakh pieces/month from Q4 FY27 and Senator/Polipluz targets, but sanitaryware utilisation is only 70% with a kiln shut and the greenfield plant timing undecided.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management targets EBITDA margin of 14-15% sustained from Q1 FY27 as discount control starts, versus 15.2% in Q4 and 10.2% in Q3; the 1-2% faucetware price-cost gap and 29-30% YoY brass rise limit upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q4 FY27 (faucetware); greenfield sanitaryware timing undecid
rows.why: Faucetware utilisation at 106% in Q4 with output of 4.3 lakh pieces/month against a move to 5 lakh pieces/month from Q4 FY27 on INR 4-5 crore capex; sanitaryware utilisation only 70% so the greenfield first phase (about INR 150 crore, land INR 27 crore bought) has no firm date.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Guided sanitaryware volume 7-8% and faucetware volume 10-12% for FY27, with Q4 volume up about 12% and retail demand recovering from Q3 into April 2026; sanitaryware output is constrained by Morbi outsourcing and 70% utilisation.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Greenfield sanitaryware first phase already estimated at INR 150 crore (up from INR 130 crore) with land bought, but construction timing depends on demand and sanitaryware utilisation is 70%, so a firm go-ahead is a demand-dependent call rather than a near-term certainty.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance of 18-20% already leans on tiles (about INR 250 crore) and Senator/Polipluz (INR 70-80 crore) versus FY26 Senator/Polipluz revenue of about INR 19 crore, and tiles are expected to be hit in Q1 FY27 by Morbi supply.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Tiles almost fully outsourced so Q1 FY27 is expected to be impacted by Morbi supply, Morbi sanitaryware output slow through monsoon, and discount control only starts Q1 FY27 with a 1-2% price-cost gap on faucetware.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Internalised Morbi-sourced sanitaryware SKUs available for sale from Q2 FY27, and Senator (40 to 60 stores) and Polipluz (200 distributors, 2,000 dealers) scaling toward INR 70-80 crore FY27 target from INR 19 crore in FY26.

rows.label: Senator and Polipluz scale-up to INR 70-80 crore
rows.why: FY26 revenue about INR 19 crore with combined losses about INR 8.5 crore; target needs Senator stores rising from 40 to 60 and Polipluz reaching 200 distributors, with management expecting profitability after publicity only in FY28.

rows.label: Price increases to recover brass cost
rows.why: Brass up about 29-30% YoY to INR 800-850/kg; 12% sanitaryware and 16% faucetware increases taken, leaving a 1-2% faucetware gap to recover via discounts, and projects lag about six months.

rows.label: Project share rising to 39-40%
rows.why: Project share rose from about 30% to 39-40% and management expects it to stabilise at a 60:40 retail-to-project split, with project pricing lagging by about six months.

tone.note: Management was confident on retail recovery from Q3 and FY27 volume guidance of 7-8% sanitaryware and 10-12% faucetware, but cautious on margins and Morbi-linked supply, stressing discount control is a gradual journey from Q1 FY27; analysts pushed on the FY27 growth bridge, Senator/Polipluz breakeve
